FAILURE example I use as a test for these LLM/AI. 
—-
If you were to combine Mercury, Venus, Mars, and Pluto into one planet in the orbit of mars, with Charon as the moon, how would that compare to earth/moon system in mass, density, size, water, etc
—-
Every single LLM/AI fails this question. The real answer is the combined mass is less than Earth — yet every LLM/AI states fake results (usually >2x more massive than Earth) , doesn’t validate the result, and has little ability to discern the objective imagined terraforming comparison for why Earth 2.0  (colonizing Mars or Luna) would be tough: gravity, water, material resources, atmosphere, magnetosphere, tides, etc.

This is a SIMPLE mathematical calculation for combined mass… with more creative determinations of water, density, gravity well, atmosphere, habitability, etc. for relative comparisons.

comments_highlight.author: @henrischomäcker
comments_highlight.text:
@KGTiberius  Absolutely true! I really had big hopes on Perplexity but the whole service/product unfortunately has the same problems that every llm has: It's simply dumb!
If you don't know that the given answers are wrong, it's unusable.
I had this scenario a few times:
One example: I asked Perplexity for a special mailserver configuration for wich I couldn't find the answer even unsing multiple search engines, but found one Page where my question was asked, but the first answer was a correct answer for a similar, question in used words but in fact a different question, the second and third answers seemed to be correct, but I tested them and they were not.
Perplexity, ChatGTP, Google's newest model and Microsoft's reacted all in the same way:
They all gave me that first answer of that page I found which was the wrong answer to my  question but the right one to a seemingly similar question with exact that page's quotation.
When I told Perplexity that that was the wrong answer and even formulated my question in a slightly other way, hoping that it would now understan, it apologized and gave me a compilation of the second two wrong answers on that page.
When I then again told it it was wrong and again explained my question far mor in detail with an example, it simply made up an answer beeing as incorrect as the others.
If I didn't already new that all of these answers were wrong I would have tested all these wrong answers as mailserver configurations and would have lost a lot of time.
The problem is simply that LLMs do not understand and they do not know that they do not know. - And that's simply because the concept how they are designed does not implement that but only predicting and maybe call it combining based on something they have been trained before.
And that's also the reason why they con not really code! - They do not understand the code.
If they now get better and better with coding it's just because they are now trained with more and better quality examples.
Imho that's also the reason why real intelligent models will not be based on LLMs, but the LLM concepts will be included for the communication part. But without another new good concept AGI or even SAI will not really be possible.
Better and better LLM's will be enough for a lot of applications, but imho not enough for that.

The problem with perplexity is that the idea for the product is eventually good but if you base a product on a tool that is not able to do the job "by design", your product can't either.
